description: We are Team PROMETHEUS, creating an interactive gateway to NASA's SPHEREx discoveries. Our website has six sections: an introduction to our team and mission; a cosmic time machine to track objects across sky images; a quiz unlocking seven discoveries; a 102-band image explorer with a 3D spacecraft model; a lab for combining six filters; and six tables explaining all 102 spectral bands. We turn complex data into an exciting journey, inviting everyone to explore how the universe changes over time.
summary: We made Prometheus to turn learning about SPHEREx into a journey through the infrared sky. Visitors can blink between images taken at different times, mark interesting points, solve seven sky puzzles, and explore the mission through a six-band guide and a 102-channel color display. Our project includes SPHEREx image cutouts with dates and source links, explanations of the mission, and a place to save exploration notes. It connects the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge with the first steps of looking carefully, comparing observations, and asking questions. We want visitors to enjoy exploring real space images and understand that noticing something interesting is the beginning of an investigation.
details:
We wanted learning about SPHEREx to feel like a journey. Prometheus brings together images, puzzles, color activities, and short explanations so visitors can explore the infrared sky step by step.

The current project includes a time-machine activity with 29 embedded image cutouts across seven targets. Visitors can blink between observations, read dates and wavelengths, and mark points in the images. Seven sky puzzles encourage careful observation. A six-band guide explains SPHEREx, while a 102-channel color activity introduces how infrared wavelengths can be displayed using visible colors. Visitors can also save exploration notes in their browser.

We used HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Canvas, embedded pages, and Three.js for a spacecraft view. Our creative idea is to connect a space journey with hands-on observation and playful activities. This supports the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge by introducing image comparison and the mission behind the observations.

The colors are learning aids, and marked points are visitor annotations. They are not calibrated spectra or proof of a moving object or a new planet. The project also contains an archive-search interface; searches for new observations require a separate server connection.

To open the project from Google Drive, download the HTML file and open it in a browser. The embedded activities are included in the file; online archive features and some external resources need internet access.
